topics.topic: Allowed caller influence over executable query and command structure
questions: Does “structure” prohibit textual interpolation entirely, or only caller control of semantic operators, identifiers and command syntax, and what evidence verifies the rule for the selected backend?
Which caller-controlled values may select predefined query or command branches, and what exact rule proves that all remaining values cannot alter interpreted structure?

Which backend lowerings satisfy this rule—for example escaped interpolation, query-builder literals, dynamic identifiers, regular expressions, paths or command arguments—and how can the invariant be verified without requiring bound parameters?

quotes: No value a caller gives ever becomes part of a query's or a command's structure; how the store's backend lowers this is the backend's.

injection_interpreted_input: no input becomes query, command, template or
     other interpreted structure;
judgement.divergence: One implementer permits escaped interpolation, dynamic identifiers and caller-selected query branches, while another permits only predefined statements with caller values bound strictly as data; callers and attackers notice different accepted inputs and injection exposure, and the owner notices different security guarantees.
judgement.why: The undefined boundary between data and structure, together with no backend-verification rule, leaves a security-relevant implementation choice open.

topics.topic: Interoperable authenticated-encryption format for backups
questions: Which authenticated-encryption construction, key derivation, nonce format, metadata authentication and key-digest algorithm define a valid backup?
What encryption, nonce, authentication and metadata-binding rules define a valid backup and prevent undetected ciphertext or metadata substitution?
What exact cryptographic format must implementations use so encryption, tamper detection and key identification are interoperable and testable?

judgement.why: This is the same backup encryption, authentication and metadata-format question previously assigned to State 6, and the relevant passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Required authenticated backup encryption format and tamper detection
quotes: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its making (A17).
A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with.
precedent.why: The algorithm, nonce, authenticated envelope, key identifier and cryptographic-version representation are encoding and file-format contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Owner-session cookie attributes and deployment rules, including local HTTP support
questions: What exact cookie attributes and deployment boundary implement “only to Registry's own origin,” given that browser cookies are scoped by host and path rather than full origin and may be sent to another port on the same host?
Which cookie attributes and deployment hostname/path make the cookie available only to Registry, including when the owner uses the interface locally?
How does Registry decide whether to issue a Secure cookie while still supporting any permitted local HTTP access?
What exact cookie attributes prevent the session from being sent in cross-site or sibling-host contexts?

judgement.why: This repeats the previously judged question about cookie attributes, scope, transport and deployment constraints on the same text.

precedent.topic: Owner-session cookie scope, attributes, and deployment constraints
quotes: The owner signs in with the owner credential (R0-30) and receives an owner session (M11), carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only to Registry's own origin.
precedent.why: Exact cookie attributes, host/path scope and SameSite transport policy are HTTP contract and encoding details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Security-review status and coverage after the A19 injection-rule change
questions: Is A21 currently reopened and awaiting a new review, or has the changed A19 wording already been reviewed and reaccepted?
What accepted rule and required tests cover templates and every other interpreted sink, and verify the backend-specific lowering that A19 now delegates?
What rules prevent caller input from becoming other interpreted structures not covered by those clauses, and does A21 remain complete after the A19 change?

judgement.why: This asks again whether A19 is covered by the performed A21 review; P5 already judged that question on unchanged passages.

precedent.topic: Reopening and rerunning the injection security review after A19 changed
quotes: A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.
Every decision a category names is accepted.
Security review: PERFORMED
- injection_interpreted_input: APPLICABLE; references: A02, A16, A19; affected: M03, M08, import file, every stored text value
- browser_boundary: APPLICABLE; references: A13, A19; affected: owner interface, CSRF protection, session cookie, rendering of agent-written text
precedent.why: The current performed and accepted A21 review expressly includes A19 in both affected categories, and the text supplies no later A19 change that would reopen it.

topics.topic: Concurrency-review coverage of confirmation consumption and imports
questions: Must A13 and its concurrent-consumption guarantee be part of the concurrency review, or is the reference list intentionally non-exhaustive?
Are confirmation consumption and concurrent import submissions within the reviewed concurrency scope, and which accepted decisions prove their behavior?

quotes:
Each outcome below answers the category's
   questions, as that catalogue states them, by naming the decisions that do,
   or, for NOT_APPLICABLE, why the category's subject is absent:

concurrency: read-check-change races, single-use values, atomic
     transitions, duplicate submissions;
- concurrency: APPLICABLE; references: A01, A04, A07, A12, A14; affected: M01, M04, M05, M06, M09, concurrent creates, corrections, publishes and session changes
judgement.why: A21 says each applicable outcome names the decisions answering all of its stated questions, but the concurrency outcome omits A13's single-use confirmation rule and A16's import transaction despite expressly claiming coverage of single-use values and duplicate submissions.

topics.topic: Controls for service-token guessing, replay, and revocation
questions: What happens when a caller repeatedly presents wrong service tokens?
Are service-token guessing and bearer-token replay intentionally accepted risks, rate-limited, or assigned to an external control, and how is a compromised token revoked?

quotes: A token not in the configuration is refused like a wrong one (R0-23).
A change of the configuration takes effect at the next start (R0-20).
judgement.divergence: One implementer permits unlimited wrong-token attempts and unrestricted reuse of a copied valid bearer token until configuration is changed and Registry restarts; another throttles wrong-token attempts or adds replay controls, which malicious callers, legitimate services and the owner observe.
judgement.why: A21 claims coverage of machine-boundary guessing, replay and abuse ownership, but the cited rules specify ordinary refusal and restart-time rotation without defining abuse controls or valid-token replay behavior.

topics.topic: Enforcement of owner-only quarantine until restore reconciliation completes
questions: What prevents service tokens from being enabled and the restored stale data served before the required reconciliation is complete?
What prevents service access from being enabled before the required erasures, restrictions and audit-date erasure have actually been restored?

quotes:
The owner first starts the restored instance owner-only (A17 rule 1), so
   no service and no agent reaches it, and brings each Customer and project to
   the state the owner's own record of the retention review (R0-60) gives for
   it now — erased, restricted, ended or not — and erases audit entries before
   the latest date the owner erased by, before configuring the tokens and
   starting it again.

This is the owner's operation (Explicit exclusions: the
   host's administration), and the owner's record is its evidence; Registry,
   which no longer holds those changes, cannot list them, enforce them or
   tell when this is done.
judgement.why: The texts deliberately assign quarantine and reconciliation enforcement to the owner's host procedure and explicitly state that Registry cannot verify completion.

topics.topic: Import-file digest algorithm and canonical byte representation
questions: Which digest algorithm and byte canonicalisation define the file identity used by confirmations, the migration closure and the audit entry?
How is the import file digest computed so that mapping, confirmation, closure and audit always identify the same file and collision substitution is infeasible?

judgement.why: This is the same import-file digest algorithm and canonical-byte-representation question previously assigned to State 6 on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Import-file digest algorithm and byte representation
quotes: The mapping names the file by its digest.
What Registry defines is the file it accepts on import; its format belongs to States 5 and 6.
precedent.why: The digest algorithm, canonical byte representation and encoded digest form are format and contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Lifetime scope of audit-sequence uniqueness across restores
questions: Must audit sequence numbers remain unique across the real lifetime of the installation, including histories discarded by restore, or only within the restored store’s current history?
Is non-reuse scoped only to the restored history, or must a number ever issued by production remain globally retired even after restoring an older backup?

quotes:
its sequence number, minted by Registry: 1 for the instance's first entry,
  then one more than the last ever written; never reused, also after old
  entries are erased (R0-66), so the log's order is the order of the numbers
  even where two entries share an instant (owner, 2026-10-31; codex round-02
  T2).

A store restored from a backup (A18) continues the history the backup
   holds: the entries written after it are lost and exist nowhere, and their
   numbers are issued again for new entries.
judgement.why: M09 says an audit sequence number is never reused after being written, while A15 expressly requires numbers lost through restoration to be issued again.

topics.topic: Atomic one-time consumption of concurrent confirmation submissions
questions: Can two concurrent submissions both pass the one-time-value check and execute, or must consumption be atomically won by exactly one submission?

topics.topic: Backup-directory isolation and safe identification of Registry files
questions: Must the backup location be dedicated to Registry, and how does Registry distinguish its backups and temporary files from unrelated files when checking and deleting them?

topics.topic: Checks required for each kind of agent-authority call
questions: Do all agent-authority calls require three checks, or do registration and non-project session operations use the stated one- and two-check exceptions?

topics.topic: Confirmation expiry behavior at the exact deadline
questions: Is a confirmation value accepted or refused at exactly its shown instant plus 10 minutes?

topics.topic: Cross-session cleanup of uploaded import files after acceptance
questions: When one owner session accepts the import, are uploaded files in all other owner sessions dropped immediately or retained until those sessions end?

topics.topic: Current checks required when replaying a create request
questions: Must a create replay pass all current lifecycle and eligibility checks, or only the reduced checks stated by A01?

topics.topic: Disclosure classification of personal data in pending import confirmations
questions: What class applies to personal-data values copied from the import file into the owner session’s pending confirmation?

topics.topic: Lifetime scope of the one-import migration rule across restores
questions: Does the one-import rule apply to the installation’s real lifetime or only to the currently restored store history?

topics.topic: Linearisation of a create retry racing a correction
questions: If a create retry races a correction of the record it originally created, what linearisation determines whether the retry returns the record or is refused for differing current facts?

topics.topic: Linearisation of reads against concurrent access revocation or session end
questions: At what exact point is a read ordered against a concurrent revocation, archive or session end?

topics.topic: Meaning and validation of audit-sequence metadata in backups
questions: Does backup metadata record the greatest entry still present, the durable last-ever-issued counter, or both, and how is a backup with no audit entries checked?

topics.topic: Project selection and authorization rules for Kernel withdrawal
questions: For a Kernel withdrawal, is authorization checked against the pointer’s project regardless of the active project, or must the pointer’s project also be active when no project id is supplied?

topics.topic: Required scope and ordering of post-restore reconciliation
questions: Which exact post-backup changes must be replayed for Customers, projects and audit retention, and in what order when prerequisite lifecycle states are absent from the restored backup?

topics.topic: Reuse and audit disambiguation of ended agent-session identities
questions: How are old audit entries naming the identity distinguished from a newly registered session with that same identity, and must Registry enforce non-reuse?

topics.topic: Source of the exact import file required to repeat migration after restore
questions: From where does the owner obtain the exact import file needed to repeat the migration after the original source and uploaded session file are gone?

topics.topic: State after both backup verification and invalid-backup deletion fail
questions: What state results when verification fails and deletion of that invalid backup also fails?

topics.topic: Storage, access, cleanup, and recovery rules for uploaded import files
questions: Where and under what access, cleanup and crash-recovery rules is the uploaded personal-data file kept during the session?

topics.topic: Whether import mapping replacements can repair missing display names
questions: If a source project has a blank or missing display name but the owner supplies a valid replacement in the mapping, is the project still malformed?

topics.topic: Whether owner-interface reads require CSRF protection
questions: Must owner-interface reads carry and pass CSRF protection, or only state-changing requests?

topics.topic: Whether restoring an older release re-enables removed artifact types
questions: After a type has been removed by a later release, may restoring an older backup under its original release make that type publishable again?

topics.topic: Whether scheduled backups run during post-restore reconciliation
questions: If the restored owner-only start occurs after 03:00 UTC, must Registry back up the unreconciled restored state and thereby create a fresh 30-day copy of data that should remain erased?

topics.topic: Which refused confirmation submissions consume or clear pending state
questions: After valid session and CSRF checks, exactly which refused submissions consume or clear the session’s pending confirmation?
